clue.text: A jar for the decrepit old thing

explanation.definitionFit: Both senses are standard: an earthenware pot, and a broken-down old person or car.

clue.text: United Nations put the stopper on the order to open champagne, perhaps?

parts.note: a cork is the stopper in a bottle

explanation.surface: The United Nations bottles something up while a celebration waits to begin.
explanation.walkthrough: The definition is an instruction: the imperative verb is what you would say to get a bottle of champagne opened.
explanation.definitionFit: Drawing the cork from a bottle is how champagne is opened, so the command form fits an order to do so.

clue.text: Composition in E after Poulenc producing great riches

indicators.note: the letter E is placed after the rearranged letters
a composition is something put together, so the composer's name is to be rearranged

parts.note: taken as written, also the musical key

explanation.surface: A piece by the French composer Poulenc in the key of E brings in a fortune.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Composition' and 'E' read like a work in E major by the French composer; in fact 'Composition' is the anagram signal and 'after' sets the lone letter at the end.
explanation.definitionFit: Opulence is lavish wealth, the display of great riches.

clue.text: The nuclear deterrent that used to be good for a toast?

definitions.meaning: The submarine-launched missile system that is Britain's nuclear deterrent

definitions.text: used to be good for a toast?
definitions.meaning: a three-pronged fork was once used to hold bread before the fire for toasting

explanation.walkthrough: The second sense plays on the word's meaning of a three-pronged fork, the old toasting fork held to the fire.
explanation.definitionFit: The British missile system carries this name, and a three-pronged fork is the literal meaning of the word.

clue.text: Complexity of letters over an instrument that wouldn't play stereo

parts.note: mono sound is single-channel, the opposite of stereo
gram is short for gramophone, a record player

explanation.surface: An old record player that can only manage single-channel sound sits beneath a jumble of letters.
explanation.walkthrough: 'over' places the first piece above the second in this down answer. A gram, short for gramophone, is an old record player.
explanation.definitionFit: A monogram is a design of interlaced initials, a complex of letters woven together.

clue.text: He's a bold northern make up? That's very fair, ma'am

indicators.note: to make up is to put together, so the letters are reassembled

explanation.surface: A brash northern man in make-up asks a lady whether that is fair.
explanation.walkthrough: 'make up' rearranges HESABOLD plus N into the answer; 'ma'am' marks that the very fair hair is a woman's.
explanation.definitionFit: Ash blonde is a very pale, greyish blonde hair colour, about as fair as hair gets.

clue.text: Caravanners ordered to move residence where labour organisers meet

parts.note: to transport is to move goods or people

explanation.surface: Travellers in caravans are told to move their home on.
explanation.walkthrough: Transport House in London was for decades the headquarters of the Labour Party and of the Transport and General Workers' Union.
explanation.definitionFit: The Labour Party and a big trade union were based at this London building, so union and party organisers met there.

clue.text: See 7
We have second thoughts and throw it all up

indicators.note: in a down answer, sending everything up turns the whole run backwards

parts.note: PS, a postscript, adds second thoughts after a letter is signed

explanation.surface: We change our minds and abandon the whole plan.
explanation.walkthrough: WE plus PS (the postscript) is WEPS; 'it all up' turns the whole run over in this down answer, and 'throw' together with 'up' gives the sense of vomiting.
explanation.definitionFit: To throw up is to vomit, and to spew is to bring food back up the same way.

clue.text: A comprehensive magazine boss given good training?

parts.note: a comprehensive is a British state secondary school
ED is short for editor, the person in charge of a magazine

explanation.surface: An all-round magazine editor has been well trained.
explanation.walkthrough: A comprehensive is a British non-selective state secondary school, so it is a school here rather than an adjective meaning thorough.
explanation.definitionFit: Someone schooled has been taught or trained, ideally well.

clue.text: She could be Hope but is called something else

indicators.note: being called something else means these letters are to take a different form

explanation.surface: A woman might be named Hope, yet she goes by another name.
explanation.walkthrough: 'is called something else' rearranges the letters of BE HOPE into another girl's name.
explanation.definitionFit: Phoebe is a woman's name, so it stands for a female, a she.

clue.text: What various inks tattoo

indicators.note: various means differing, so these letters are put into a different order

explanation.surface: A question about the surface that coloured inks are pricked into.
explanation.walkthrough: 'various' rearranges INKS, and the whole clue describes where a tattooist's inks go.
explanation.definitionFit: Tattoo ink is pricked into the body's outer covering.

clue.text: Bristling to shift a nasty web in the north chamber

indicators.note: one piece goes inside the joined pair that surrounds it
nasty suggests a mess, so the letters of web are jumbled

explanation.surface: Someone is itching to clear an ugly cobweb from a room on the north side.
explanation.walkthrough: A new broom is a newcomer keen to make changes, from the proverb 'a new broom sweeps clean', so 'Bristling to shift' describes a brush eager to sweep.
explanation.definitionFit: A newcomer eager to make sweeping changes is said to sweep clean, like a fresh brush full of bristles.

clue.text: Not the main role of the actor

definitions.text: Not the main role of the actor

parts.words: Not the main role of the actor
parts.note: a small supporting role in a play rather than the lead

explanation.definitionFit: A small part in a play is a lesser role, the opposite of the lead.

clue.text: Solid food preserved and drunk

definitions.meaning: food kept in vinegar or brine, such as onions or gherkins

explanation.definitionFit: Food kept in vinegar has been preserved this way, and the word is also slang for intoxicated.

clue.text: Get a huge diamond with a crooked iron hook

indicators.note: crooked means bent out of shape, so these letters are rearranged

explanation.surface: A thief plans to land a large gem using a bent iron hook.
explanation.walkthrough: 'crooked' rearranges IRONHOOK. The Koh-i-Noor is a famous large diamond among the British Crown Jewels.
explanation.definitionFit: The Koh-i-Noor is one of the largest cut diamonds known, set in the British crown.

clue.text: Platitudinous speech about a young wife holding Order of Merit

indicators.note: holding means the first piece contains the second within it

parts.note: a bride is a newly married wife
OM is the abbreviation for the Order of Merit, a British honour

explanation.surface: A dull speech is made about a newlywed who has received a high honour.
explanation.walkthrough: The Order of Merit is a select British honour. Bromide, once a common sedative, came to mean a soothing commonplace remark.
explanation.definitionFit: A bromide is a trite, soothing remark, named after the sedative drug.

clue.text: Censure a big human settlement for greed

parts.note: to rap is to rebuke or censure
a city is a large town

explanation.surface: Condemn a large town for its avarice.
explanation.definitionFit: Rapacity is grasping greed, an eagerness to seize what others have.

clue.text: Cause bewilderment if my sty's untidy

indicators.note: untidy means disordered, so the letters are rearranged

parts.note: the possessive sty's gives sty, with no extra letter

explanation.surface: Someone is baffled at how messy a pigsty can get.
explanation.walkthrough: 'untidy' rearranges IFMYSTY; the 's of sty's adds no letter.
explanation.definitionFit: To mystify is to puzzle or baffle someone completely.

clue.text: Just like a matron as she manages Tory helm

indicators.note: manages suggests handling and reworking, so the letters are rearranged

explanation.surface: A woman is like a hospital matron as she runs the Conservative party.
explanation.definitionFit: A matron is a mature, caring woman, so behaving like one is maternal and caring.

clue.text: A shoal thrown free

indicators.note: thrown means flung about, so these letters are scattered into a new order

explanation.surface: A school of fish is cast loose.
explanation.walkthrough: 'shoal' suggests fish, but here it is shallow water over a ridge of rock; 'thrown' rearranges FREE.
explanation.definitionFit: A shoal is a sandbank or shallow, a hazard to shipping like a ridge of rock near the surface.

clue.text: A fill of tobacco for the boatswain?

definitions.meaning: a ... of tobacco is one bowlful
a boatswain's ... is the whistle used to give orders on deck

explanation.definitionFit: One smoke from a bowl filled with tobacco is a pipeful, and a ship's boatswain blows a shrill whistle of the same name.

clue.text: He'll skin the old Bobby

definitions.meaning: one who takes the skin off fruit or vegetables
an old slang word for a policeman, after Sir Robert Peel

explanation.walkthrough: Robert Peel founded the London police, whose officers were nicknamed both bobbies and peelers after him.
explanation.definitionFit: A person or tool stripping skin off fruit is one sense; the other is old slang for police officers, named after Sir Robert Peel.

clue.text: Ruler crossing the sea

explanation.definitionFit: A tool for drawing straight lines is one sense, and a large ocean passenger ship is the other.

clue.text: The hanger-on to cause unpleasant odour in the Home Counties

indicators.note: in places the smell inside the region

parts.note: SE, South East, stands for the counties around London
to pong is British slang for to stink

explanation.surface: A freeloader makes a bad smell in the counties around London.
explanation.walkthrough: The Home Counties are the English counties surrounding London, in the South East; PONG is British slang for a stink.
explanation.definitionFit: A sponger lives off others, a parasite who hangs on for free meals.

clue.text: Had a good meal so less likely to fall out

definitions.meaning: to tuck in is to eat heartily
a shirt or child secured under trousers or bedclothes

explanation.definitionFit: Eating heartily is tucking in, and a shirt pushed into trousers or a child under blankets is held secure.

clue.text: Convincing evidence that the picture was taken

definitions.meaning: a trial print of a photograph

explanation.definitionFit: Evidence that establishes a fact is one sense; a trial print from a photographer is the other.

clue.text: Ready to wear an unmeasured wardrobe

definitions.meaning: clothes bought from a rail without being made to measure

explanation.definitionFit: Ready-made clothes hang on a rail in the shop rather than being tailored.
